taxonomy.note: GBIF match accepted Emberiza schoeniclus at species rank; its backbone supplies the family and genus used by the schema.

external.note: GBIF usage key 2491557 resolves to accepted Emberiza schoeniclus. Current iNaturalist species taxon 1720562 is accepted as Schoeniclus schoeniclus; the genus differs, and iNaturalist taxon 9201 is inactive with 1720562 as its current synonym.

range.note: The article says the species breeds throughout Europe; GB is supported as a native breeding region.

traits.limb_count.note: Bird legs only; wings are excluded from this count by the schema.

traits.locomotion_modes.note: Flight is stated in the article. Hop is an authored movement mapping for the described ground-feeding bird; the source establishes foraging near the ground, not a measured gait.

traits.thermoregulation.note: Endothermy is the standard avian trait mapping.

traits.nest_type.note: Nest described in a bush or reed tussock; represented as a ground nest.

traits.perching.note: Judgement: a perch pose is an authored action for this passerine; the cited species article supports male song but does not specify the song posture.

traits.size_class.note: Tiny follows the schema's less-than-0.05 kg threshold.

traits.mass_kg.note: Midpoint of the stated 10-28 g adult range, converted to 0.019 kg; not a population mean.

traits.mass_range_kg.note: The article states 10-28 g, converted to 0.010-0.028 kg.

traits.length_m.note: Midpoint of the stated 13.5-15.5 cm range, converted to 0.145 m.

traits.lifespan_y.note: Low-confidence expected-age proxy, not a directly measured lifespan. CSV ELEscholer2020_data.csv line 110 (dataset row X=124) reports annual adult survival 0.48 (SE 0.02), UK, mark-recapture, Clark et al. 2011. Assuming a constant adult mortality hazard and first breeding at age 1 y, 1 + (-1 / ln(0.48)) = 2.36 y, stored as 2.4 y. This conditions on reaching breeding age and excludes juvenile mortality.

traits.diet.note: The article says adults take insects when feeding young and seeds otherwise. The equal split is an authored simulation allocation, not a measured diet proportion.

traits.social.note: Monogamy supports a representative pair; group size is the pair unit, not a flock estimate.

traits.activity_pattern.note: Judgement: diurnal is an authored bird activity mapping; no species-specific night survey was located.

traits.defense.note: The article describes flight and nesting in cover; the flee response is an authored simulation choice.

habitat.use.note: The sources describe ground feeding and low nests plus perches in reeds; 0.8 ground / 0.2 arboreal is an authored allocation.

habitat.shelter_tag.note: Reed tussocks and bushes are represented with the available shrub_thicket shelter tag.

habitat.resources.note: The tags follow seed/insect foods and nests in bushes or reed tussocks. Weights are authored; seasonal food availability follows the reported diet switch during chick feeding.

habitat.human_tolerance.note: Judgement: Avoider for the wetland and open-field habitat represented here.

seasonal.strategy.note: The article describes migration overall and resident populations in the milder south and west. This GB-only model uses ActiveYearRound for individuals present across the year; migrant fractions and upland departures are not represented.

seasonal.phases.note: GB breeding period approximate bounds from early April through late August.

seasonal.life_stages.note: Adult-only lifecycle entry; juvenile development is not modeled in this record.

activity.regions.note: GB, tier A (CC0/CC BY) on both providers, combined normalized monthly shares. iNaturalist total 2,937 with per-month counts 220, 231, 370, 495, 429, 382, 208, 94, 89, 147, 120, 152; GBIF total 403,028 with every monthly bin above 17,000. Low iNaturalist August-October bins are outweighed by the robust GBIF series. Occurrence frequency is a detectability proxy, not direct activity measurement.

behavior.note: Species-local program keeps ground feeding, the reported seed/invertebrate diet switch, nesting in months 4-8, and male song in that breeding window. Elevated reed perching and hop gait are authored movement choices, not directly measured actions. Song and feeding are day-only; at night the tree rests in shrub cover after threat/fear branches.

vocalizations.song.note: Article describes the male's repetitive 'srip' song. The April-August season follows the breeding window and is an authored restriction.

look.note: Adult male black head/throat with white collar, barred brown back and pale underside; block proportions, patch sizes and simplified male-only plumage are judgement.
